description: You are a Health Informatics Specialist at City General Hospital. The Laboratory Information System (LIS) sends HL7 ORU^R01 result messages for all tests. Clinicians have been missing life-threatening critical value alerts because all results land in the same destination. Build a NextGen Connect channel named 'Lab Critical Value Router' that: (1) Listens on TCP port 6664 for HL7 ORU^R01 messages using MLLP framing. (2) Contains a JavaScript transformer that iterates over ALL OBX segments in the message and checks OBX-8 (Abnormal Flags field) for critical indicators 'HH' (high critical) or 'LL' (low critical), then sets a channel map variable 'isCritical' to 'true' if any critical OBX is found. (3) Has a first Database Writer destination named 'Critical DB Writer' with a filter that only passes when 'isCritical' equals 'true', INSERTing into a PostgreSQL table 'critical_lab_results' (columns: message_id VARCHAR, patient_mrn VARCHAR, test_code VARCHAR, test_value VARCHAR, abnormal_flag VARCHAR, observation_time VARCHAR, received_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()). (4) Has a second Database Writer destination named 'Normal DB Writer' with a filter that only passes when 'isCritical' does NOT equal 'true', INSERTing into a PostgreSQL table 'normal_lab_results' (same column structure). (5) Has a third File Writer destination named 'Audit Log Writer' with NO filter (always fires) that writes ALL messages to /tmp/lab_audit/ inside the container. (6) The channel must be deployed and in STARTED state. Sample messages: /home/ga/sample_critical_oru.hl7 (has OBX-8=HH), /home/ga/sample_normal_oru.hl7 (all OBX-8=N). Both PostgreSQL tables must be created before or by the channel. PostgreSQL is accessible from inside the NextGen Connect container at jdbc:postgresql://nextgen-postgres:5432/mirthdb (username: postgres, password: postgres). You may create the tables manually via: docker exec nextgen-postgres psql -U postgres -d mirthdb -c 'CREATE TABLE ...' The REST API is at https://localhost:8443/api (credentials: admin/admin). All REST API calls require the header 'X-Requested-With: OpenAPI'. The web dashboard at https://localhost:8443 is monitoring-only.
